advances: Strict arithmetic improvement for finite monotone weights, with sharpness across support lengths. It does not infer reflection of the spatial fibers.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Write $S_i=\sum_{h\ge i}w_h$ and choose the largest $j$ with $S_j\ge M/2$. If $j=0$, then $S_1<M/2$ and $B_0=w_0>M/2$. For $N\ge2$, $w_N\le M/3$ by monotonicity, so $j<N$. For $j\ge1$ both $S_j,S_{j+1}$ are positive. Monotonicity also gives
$$
B_j=w_j+2\sum_{h=1}^j w_{j+h}=S_j+S_{j+1}-2S_{2j+1}.
$$
With $a=S_j/M$, $b=S_{j+1}/M$, and $c=S_{2j+1}/M$, the strict finite survival bound at indices $j,j+1$ gives $c<ab$. Since $a\ge1/2>b$, the identity $B_j/M-1/2=(a-1/2)(1-2b)+2(ab-c)$ proves the strict result. For $N=1$, the only occupied centers are $0,1$, whose reflected masses are respectively $w_0,w_1$, while all other centers have zero reflected mass. The maximum equals half the total exactly when they are equal. For $N=0$ the sole occupied center retains the whole mass.

statement: Let $w_0\ge\cdots\ge w_N>0$ be log-concave and zero outside its support. Write $M=\sum_iw_i$ and $B_j=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}\min(w_i,w_{2j-i})$. Then $\max_{j\in\mathbb Z}B_j>M/2$ when $N\ge2$. When $N=1$ the maximum equals $M/2$ exactly when $w_0=w_1$, and when $N=0$ it equals $M$. In particular the constant $1/2$ is sharp.
title: Strict monotone median reflection and its equality case
